ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within square $ABCD$, point $E$ is on diagonal $AC$, $EF \perp AB$ at point $F$, $EG \perp BC$ at point $G$. Connect $FG$. If $AB = 8$, what is the minimum value of $FG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect BE, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore \angle B=90^\circ$, AB=BC=8, \\
$\therefore$AC=8$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\because$EF$\perp$AB, EG$\perp$BC, \\
$\therefore \angle$BFE=$\angle$FEG=$\angle$B=$90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral BFEG is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$FG=BE, \\
$\therefore$ When BE is the shortest, FG is also the shortest, \\
$\therefore$ When BE$\perp$AC, BE is the shortest, \\
$\therefore$AE=CE, \\
$\therefore$BE=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=4$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of FG is $\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Geometric distance-to-line route. First read the diagram: B is the lower-left vertex of square ABCD, AC is the diagonal from upper-left to lower-right, E moves along AC, and F and G are the perpendicular feet from E to the left and bottom sides, making BFEG visually a rectangle with FG as one diagonal. From the text, AB=BC=8 and EF ⟂ AB, EG ⟂ BC. Since AB ⟂ BC, the four right angles imply BFEG is a rectangle, so its diagonals are equal: FG=BE. Thus minimizing FG is equivalent to minimizing BE while E moves along line segment AC. The shortest distance from fixed point B to line AC occurs at the perpendicular from B to AC. In square ABCD, triangle ABC is right isosceles with legs 8, so AC=8sqrt(2), and the altitude from the right angle B to hypotenuse AC is AC/2=4sqrt(2). Therefore the minimum value of FG is 4sqrt(2).

Reasoning: According to the coordinate optimization method, let B=(0,0), A=(0,8), C=(8,0), D=(8,8). Because E is on diagonal AC, E can be set as E=(t,8-t), where 0≤t≤8. From the projection relationship in the figure, F is on AB and is horizontal with E, so F=(0,8-t); G is on BC and is vertical with E, so G=(t,0). Thus FG²=(t-0)²+(0-(8-t))²=t²+(8-t)²=2(t-4)²+32. This quadratic expression attains the minimum value 32 when t=4, therefore the minimum value of FG is √32=4√2.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within square $ABCD$, point $E$ is on diagonal $AC$, $EF \perp AB$ at point $F$, $EG \perp BC$ at point $G$. Connect $FG$. If $AB = 8$, what is the minimum value of $FG$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect BE, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore \angle B=90^\circ$, AB=BC=8, \\
$\therefore$AC=8$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\because$EF$\perp$AB, EG$\perp$BC, \\
$\therefore \angle$BFE=$\angle$FEG=$\angle$B=$90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral BFEG is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$FG=BE, \\
$\therefore$ When BE is the shortest, FG is also the shortest, \\
$\therefore$ When BE$\perp$AC, BE is the shortest, \\
$\therefore$AE=CE, \\
$\therefore$BE=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=4$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of FG is $\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$
